DK26.2 is a specific medical diagnosis code used within the Danish healthcare system to identify an acute duodenal ulcer accompanied by both hemorrhage and perforation. In the context of national clinical quality monitoring, this code is a critical component of the quality indicators used by the Database for Atrial Fibrillation in Denmark, which is coordinated by the Regions' Clinical Quality Development Programme (RKKP). 

Specifically, DK26.2 is utilized to measure the incidence of severe bleeding among patients treated for [[atrieflimren]] [^src1]. Because atrial fibrillation patients are frequently managed with anticoagulant therapies, tracking severe hemorrhagic events is a vital patient safety and quality-of-care metric. To ensure comprehensive surveillance, the clinical database employs a wide array of ICD-10-DK codes to capture all severe bleeding events. DK26.2 is grouped within the gastrointestinal bleeding codes (spanning DK25.0–DK29.8A and DK92.0–DK92.2), alongside codes for intracranial hemorrhages (such as [[di60|DI60]]–[[ds066|DS066]]) and urinary or respiratory tract bleeding (including [[dj942|DJ942]], [[dn02|DN02]], [[dr04|DR04]], and [[dr31|DR31]]) [^src1]. 

The methodological definitions for these indicators, including the explicit inclusion of DK26.2, are standardized and consistently published in the annual methodology reports for the atrial fibrillation database, appearing in both the 2023 and 2024 documentation [^src1] [^src2].
